main_text.p: conicæ reipublicæ hanc Carthaginien-sem comparat, & ex regio & optima-tum ac populi statu compositam tem-peratamque olim fuisse ostendit, Suffe-tes regum instar fuisse, senatum opti-matum locum tenuisse, populum sibi convenientem, aut rerum sibi compe-tentium, potestatem habuisse censet.

Verba ejus sic habent : χρὴ γὰρ βασιλέως [illegible, ~8 letters] παρ᾽ αὐτῆς, ἢ τὸ γερόντων εἶχε [?] [illegible, ~20 letters] τῶν ἀρχόντων ἐξέστω, ἐ τὸ πλῆθος [illegible, ~12 letters] [?] ὑπὸ τῶν πολιτῶν αὐτῷ.

Sed idem subjicit paulò post, eo tempore, quo Hannibal bellum Romanis intulit, quod fuit centum annis Aristotelis morte posterius, rempublicam Carthaginiensem à pristino & recto statu suo deflexisse, atque ideò etiam in declarationibus plurimam potestatem populum sibi sumpsisse, cum apud Romanos senatus autoritas tum adhuc esset integra, atque hoc rebus Romanis non parum profuisse, Punicis obfuisse arbitrari se demonstrat. Sed quarum rerum potestas olim in statu integro penes populum fuerit, nusquàm aperit iis in libris & fragmentis, quorum copiam nos hodiè habemus. Suspicari libet, suffragiorum jus in creandis magistratibus, in scisscendis legibus, fæderi-bus

page.notes: The Greek sentence after "Verba ejus sic habent" is set in small type and is only partly legible on the scan; the words marked [illegible] could not be read letter by letter, and the other Greek is uncertain. The faint marks at the bottom right, beside the catchword, look like bleed-through or stray marks and were left out. The word "fæderi-" is hyphenated at the end of the page and continues on the next page with "bus", which is the catchword.
